items.q: Under R.A. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004), who issues a Barangay Protection Order (BPO), and for how long is it effective?
choices: The Regional Trial Court; effective for 30 days
The barangay secretary; effective until revoked
The Punong Barangay; effective for 15 days
The municipal mayor; effective for 60 days
items.why: Sec. 14: a BPO is 'the protection order issued by the Punong Barangay ordering the perpetrator to desist' from certain acts, issued on the date of filing after ex parte determination, and 'BPOs shall be effective for fifteen (15) days.' If the Punong Barangay is unavailable, any available Barangay Kagawad may act on the application.

items.q: A jail officer claims that torturing a detainee is justified because the country faces a threat of war. What does R.A. 9745 (Anti-Torture Act of 2009) provide?
choices: Torture is allowed during a declared state of war
Torture is allowed if a superior approves it in writing
A state of war, a threat of war, or any other public emergency can never be invoked as a justification for torture
Torture is allowed only against persons named in an order of battle
items.why: Sec. 6 treats freedom from torture as an absolute right and states: 'A state of war or a threat of war, internal political instability, or any other public emergency, or a document or any determination comprising an "order of battle" shall not and can never be invoked as a justification for torture'.

items.q: Under R.A. 9745, a confession obtained as a result of torture is inadmissible in evidence in any proceeding, with one exception. What is it?
choices: When the confession is later sworn to before a notary public
When it is used as evidence against a person or persons accused of committing torture
When the confession concerns a heinous crime
When the accused was later assisted by counsel
items.why: Sec. 8: 'Any confession, admission or statement obtained as a result of torture shall be inadmissible in evidence in any proceedings, except if the same is used as evidence against a person or persons accused of committing torture.' Neither the seriousness of the crime nor later notarization makes it admissible against the victim.

items.q: Under R.A. 9851 (Philippine Act on Crimes Against International Humanitarian Law, Genocide, and Other Crimes Against Humanity), who is a person "hors de combat"?
choices: A journalist covering an armed conflict
A commander who has effective authority and control over troops
A foreign volunteer fighting for an organized armed group
A person who is in the power of an adverse party, has clearly expressed an intention to surrender, or has been rendered unconscious or otherwise incapacitated by wounds or sickness
items.why: Sec. 3(k) defines 'Hors de Combat' as a person who '(1) is in the power of an adverse party; (2) has clearly expressed an intention to surrender; or (3) has been rendered unconscious or otherwise incapacitated by wounds or sickness and therefore is incapable of defending himself', provided the person refrains from hostile acts and does not try to escape. Effective command and control is a separate term in Sec. 3(f).

items.q: Under R.A. 10353 (Anti-Enforced or Involuntary Disappearance Act of 2012), an enforced or involuntary disappearance is considered a continuing offense for as long as:
choices: the family of the victim has not filed a complaint
the perpetrators continue to conceal the fate and whereabouts of the disappeared person and these have not been determined with certainty
the perpetrators remain in government service
no court has issued a writ of amparo
items.why: Sec. 21: the act 'shall be considered a continuing offense as long as the perpetrators continue to conceal the fate and whereabouts of the disappeared person and such circumstances have not been determined with certainty.' Sec. 3(b) defines the offense as deprivation of liberty by agents of the State (or with State support) followed by refusal to acknowledge it or concealment of the person's fate.

items.q: Art. II, Sec. 16 of the 1987 Constitution directs the State to protect and advance the right of the people to:
choices: a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature
free and unlimited use of all natural resources
own lands of the public domain without limit
items.why: Art. II, Sec. 16 states: 'The State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.' The same words open the policy sections of the Clean Air Act (R.A. 8749, Sec. 2) and the Climate Change Act (R.A. 9729, Sec. 2).

items.q: Under R.A. 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000), where shall a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) be established?
choices: In every barangay or cluster of barangays
In every region, under DENR management
items.why: Sec. 32: 'There shall be established a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) in every barangay or cluster of barangays.' The MRF 'shall receive mixed waste for final sorting, segregation, composting, and recycling', and the residual wastes go to a long-term storage or disposal facility or sanitary landfill.

items.q: Under Sec. 20 of R.A. 9003, each local government unit's plan must show that, within five years after the law took effect, the LGU will divert at least what share of all solid waste from waste disposal facilities?
items.why: Sec. 20: 'within five (5) years after the effectivity of this Act, the LGU shall divert at least 25% of all solid waste from waste disposal facilities through re-use, recycling and composting activities and other resource recovery activities', and the diversion goals 'shall be increased every three (3) years thereafter.'

items.q: R.A. 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999) bans incineration, defined as the burning of municipal, biomedical and hazardous waste which emits poisonous and toxic fumes. Which of the following does Sec. 20 expressly exclude from the ban?
choices: The traditional small-scale method of community or neighborhood sanitation called "siga"
Burning of mixed municipal garbage at a city dumpsite
Burning of plastic waste by factories
Burning of all hospital waste in new incinerators
items.why: Sec. 20 provides that 'the prohibition shall not apply to traditional small-scale method of community/neighborhood sanitation "siga", traditional, agricultural, cultural, health, and food preparation and crematoria.' Burning municipal or industrial waste is exactly what the ban covers.

items.q: Under R.A. 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004), the wastewater charge system is established on the basis of what?
choices: A flat annual tax on all households
Payments by the government to industries that reduce pollution
Payment to the government for discharging wastewater into the water bodies
items.why: Sec. 13: 'The system shall be established on the basis of payment to the government for discharging wastewater into the water bodies.' One purpose of the charges is 'To provide strong economic inducement for polluters to modify their production or management processes or to invest in pollution control technology'.

items.q: Under R.A. 9729 (Climate Change Act of 2009), which are the frontline agencies in the formulation, planning and implementation of climate change action plans in their respective areas?
choices: The regional offices of the DENR
The provincial offices of the Department of Science and Technology
items.why: Sec. 14: 'The LGUs shall be the frontline agencies in the formulation, planning and implementation of climate change action plans in their respective areas, consistent with the provisions of the Local Government Code, the Framework, and the National Climate Change Action Plan.'

items.q: Under R.A. 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act), which department has jurisdiction over the dugong (outside Palawan)?
choices: The Department of Agriculture, because the dugong is a marine mammal
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources
The Department of the Interior and Local Government
items.why: Sec. 4 gives the DENR jurisdiction over 'all terrestrial plant and animal species, all turtles and tortoises and wetland species, including but not limited to crocodiles, waterbirds and all amphibians and dugong', while the DA covers 'all marine mammals, except dugong.' In Palawan, this jurisdiction is vested in the Palawan Council for Sustainable Development.

items.q: Under the Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System Act of 2018 (R.A. 11038), what are "buffer zones"?
choices: Core areas inside a protected area where no human entry is allowed
Areas inside a protected area where settlement and sustainable livelihood activities may be allowed
Coastal areas no deeper than six meters at low tide
Identified areas outside the boundaries of and immediately adjacent to designated protected areas that need special development control to avoid or minimize harm to the protected area
items.why: R.A. 11038, Sec. 3, amending Sec. 4(c) of R.A. 7586, defines buffer zones as 'identified areas outside the boundaries of and immediately adjacent to designated protected areas that need special development control in order to avoid or minimize harm to the protected area.' Areas inside where settlement and livelihood may be allowed are multiple-use zones (Sec. 4(t)).

items.q: What is 3/4 + 5/6?
items.why: Use the common denominator 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12, so the sum is 19/12 = 1 7/12. The trap 8/10 comes from adding numerators and denominators separately, and 15/24 comes from multiplying instead of adding.

items.q: Evaluate: 48 − 6 × 5 + 12 ÷ 4
items.why: Multiply and divide first: 6 × 5 = 30 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Then 48 − 30 + 3 = 21. Working left to right without the order of operations gives 55.5, and subtracting the sum (48 − 33) gives 15.

items.q: What is 2.5 × 0.04?
items.why: 25 × 4 = 100, and the factors have 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places, so the product is 0.100 = 0.1. Counting only two decimal places gives 1, and counting four gives 0.01.

items.q: What is 35% of 240?
items.why: 10% of 240 is 24, so 30% is 72 and 5% is 12; 72 + 12 = 84. 72 is only 30%, and 8.4 comes from misplacing the decimal point.

items.q: 15 is what percent of 60?
items.why: 15 ÷ 60 = 1/4 = 25%. Dividing the other way (60 ÷ 15 = 4) leads to 4%, and 75% is the part of 60 that is not 15.
A negative times a negative is positive: (−8) × (−3) = 24. Subtracting a negative means adding: 24 − (−5) = 24 + 5 = 29. Treating "− (−5)" as "− 5" gives the trap answer 19.

items.q: What is 7.2 ÷ 0.08?
items.why: Move both decimal points two places to the right: 7.2 ÷ 0.08 = 720 ÷ 8 = 90. Misreading 0.08 as 0.8 gives 9, and as 0.008 gives 900.
Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 2/3 × 9/4 = 18/12 = 3/2 = 1 1/2. Multiplying the fractions directly (2/3 × 4/9) gives the trap 8/27.

items.q: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 2 : 5, what is a : c?
items.why: Make the b terms equal: b : c = 2 : 5 = 4 : 10, so a : b : c = 3 : 4 : 10 and a : c = 3 : 10. Simply pairing the first and last numbers (3 : 5) ignores that b has different values in the two ratios.
Parentheses first (10 − 4 = 6), then the exponent (3² = 9), then 9 × 2 = 18 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2. So 5 + 18 − 2 = 21. Adding 5 + 9 before multiplying gives 26, and forgetting to divide 6 by 3 gives 17.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.375?
items.why: 0.375 = 375/1000; dividing both by 125 gives 3/8. 3/5 = 0.6 and 5/8 = 0.625 come from guessing from the digits, and 7/20 = 0.35 is close but not equal.

items.q: Which of the following has the greatest value?
items.why: Convert all to decimals: 5/8 = 0.625, 0.61, 62% = 0.62, and 7/12 is about 0.583. The greatest is 5/8. 62% is the tempting choice because it looks like the largest number, but 0.62 is less than 0.625.

items.q: A price goes up from ₱80 to ₱100. What is the percent increase?
items.why: Percent increase = increase ÷ original = 20 ÷ 80 = 25%. Dividing by the new price (20 ÷ 100 = 20%) is the common mistake, and 125% is the new price as a percent of the old one.

Convert to twelfths: 5 1/4 = 63/12 and 2 2/3 = 32/12, so the difference is 31/12 = 2 7/12. Subtracting the smaller fraction from the larger (2/3 − 1/4 = 5/12) and writing 3 5/12 is the usual trap; you must borrow 1 from the whole number.
(0.5)² = 0.25 and 1/4 × 0.8 = 0.2, so 0.25 + 0.2 − 0.1 = 0.35. Adding 0.25 + 1/4 before multiplying gives 0.3, and treating (0.5)² as 0.5 gives 0.6.

items.q: What is the next number? 7, 12, 17, 22, ___
items.why: Each term is 5 more than the one before: 22 + 5 = 27. 32 would mean adding 10, which does not fit any step in the series.

items.q: What is the next number? 95, 88, 81, 74, ___
items.why: The series goes down by 7 each time: 74 − 7 = 67. 60 subtracts 14, which skips a term.

items.q: What is the next number? 2, 6, 18, 54, ___
items.why: Each term is multiplied by 3: 54 × 3 = 162. 108 doubles 54 instead of tripling it, and 72 adds 18 as if the series were arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next number? 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ___
items.why: These are the perfect squares 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², so the next is 6² = 36. The differences 3, 5, 7, 9 also point to +11. 30 adds 5 again, which ignores the growing differences.

items.q: What is the next number? 5, 7, 11, 17, 25, ___
items.why: The differences are 2, 4, 6, 8, so the next difference is 10: 25 + 10 = 35. 33 repeats the last difference of 8.

items.q: What is the next number? 4, 8, 6, 12, 10, 20, ___
items.why: The rule alternates "multiply by 2" and "subtract 2": 4 × 2 = 8, 8 − 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, 12 − 2 = 10, 10 × 2 = 20, so next is 20 − 2 = 18. 40 doubles twice in a row and breaks the alternation.

items.q: What is the next number? 3, 20, 6, 18, 9, 16, 12, ___
items.why: Two series are interleaved. The 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th terms go 3, 6, 9, 12 (+3), and the 2nd, 4th, 6th terms go 20, 18, 16 (−2). The 8th term belongs to the second series: 16 − 2 = 14. 15 continues the wrong series (12 + 3).

items.q: What is the next number? 1, 50, 2, 45, 4, 40, 8, ___
items.why: Odd-position terms double (1, 2, 4, 8) and even-position terms drop by 5 (50, 45, 40). The next term is in the even-position series: 40 − 5 = 35. 16 is the trap: it is the next term of the doubling series, which comes one place later.

items.q: What is the next number? 81, 27, 9, 3, ___
items.why: Each term is divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1. 0 and −3 assume a subtraction pattern, which does not fit 81 to 27.

items.q: What is the next number? 1, 8, 27, 64, ___
items.why: These are cubes: 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, so the next is 5³ = 125. 100 and 81 are squares (10² and 9²), and 216 = 6³ skips a term.

items.q: What number is missing? 2, 5, ___, 17, 26, 37
items.why: Each term is a perfect square plus 1: 1+1, 4+1, 9+1, 16+1, 25+1, 36+1. The missing term is 9 + 1 = 10. The differences 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 confirm it (5 + 5 = 10 and 10 + 7 = 17).

items.q: What is the next number? 5, 10, 13, 26, 29, ___
items.why: The rule alternates "multiply by 2" and "add 3": 5 × 2 = 10, 10 + 3 = 13, 13 × 2 = 26, 26 + 3 = 29, so next is 29 × 2 = 58. 32 adds 3 twice in a row.

items.q: Aling Rosa buys 3 dozen eggs at ₱90 per dozen and sells every egg at ₱9 each. What is her total profit if she sells all the eggs?
items.why: Cost: 3 × ₱90 = ₱270. Sales: 36 eggs × ₱9 = ₱324. Profit: ₱324 − ₱270 = ₱54. ₱18 is the profit on only one dozen, and ₱324 is the total sales, not the profit.

items.q: A rice cooker is priced at ₱2,400. During a sale it is offered at 15% off. What is the sale price?
items.why: 15% of ₱2,400 = ₱360, so the sale price is ₱2,400 − ₱360 = ₱2,040. ₱360 is only the discount, and ₱2,385 subtracts ₱15 instead of 15%.

items.q: A school bag tagged at ₱1,500 is sold with a 20% discount, and members get an additional 10% off the discounted price. How much does a member pay?
items.why: After 20% off: ₱1,500 × 0.80 = ₱1,200. Another 10% off: ₱1,200 × 0.90 = ₱1,080. Adding the discounts to get 30% off (₱1,050) is the trap, because the 10% is taken from the already reduced price.

items.q: A cooperative lends ₱20,000 to a member at 6% simple interest per year. How much interest is due after 2 years and 6 months?
items.why: Simple interest = principal × rate × time = ₱20,000 × 0.06 × 2.5 = ₱3,000. Using 2 years gives ₱2,400, and ₱23,000 is the total amount (principal plus interest), not the interest.

items.q: A deposit of ₱15,000 earns ₱1,800 in simple interest after 3 years. What is the annual interest rate?
items.why: Rate = interest ÷ (principal × time) = ₱1,800 ÷ (₱15,000 × 3) = ₱1,800 ÷ ₱45,000 = 0.04 = 4%. Forgetting to divide by the 3 years gives 12%, which is the total over three years.

items.q: Kiko can paint the barangay hall fence alone in 6 hours. Lito can paint it alone in 12 hours. Working together at these rates, how long will they take?
items.why: Kiko does 1/6 of the job per hour and Lito 1/12, together 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 per hour, so the job takes 4 hours. 9 hours is the average of 6 and 12, which would be slower than Kiko working alone.

items.q: An inlet pipe can fill a water tank in 4 hours, and a drain can empty the full tank in 6 hours. If the tank starts empty and both are open, how long will it take to fill the tank?
items.why: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12 of the tank per hour, so filling takes 12 hours. Adding the rates (1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12, about 2.4 hours) is the trap: the drain works against the pipe.

items.q: A jeepney travels 45 km from Barangay Dalisay to the town proper at an average speed of 30 km per hour. How long is the trip?
items.why: Time = distance ÷ speed = 45 ÷ 30 = 1.5 hours = 1 hour 30 minutes. Reading 1.5 hours as "1 hour 50 minutes" is the common error; half an hour is 30 minutes.

items.q: A bus travels the first 60 km of a trip at 60 km per hour and the next 60 km at 40 km per hour. What is its average speed for the whole 120 km?
items.why: Time for the first part: 60 ÷ 60 = 1 hour; second part: 60 ÷ 40 = 1.5 hours. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 120 ÷ 2.5 = 48 km per hour. Averaging the two speeds (50) is wrong because the bus spends more time at the slower speed.

items.q: Mrs. Dimaculangan is now 4 times as old as her son. In 20 years, she will be twice as old as her son. How old is Mrs. Dimaculangan now?
items.why: Let the son be s, so the mother is 4s. In 20 years: 4s + 20 = 2(s + 20), so 4s + 20 = 2s + 40 and s = 10. The mother is 4 × 10 = 40. 10 is the son's age and 60 is the mother's age 20 years from now.

items.q: The sum of the ages of Ben and his sister is 30. Ben is 6 years older than his sister. How old is Ben?
items.why: Sister = x, Ben = x + 6, so 2x + 6 = 30 and x = 12. Ben is 12 + 6 = 18. 12 is the sister's age, and 24 adds 6 to 18 by mistake.

items.q: A canteen has 12 liters of a juice drink that is 25% concentrate. How many liters of water must be added so that the drink becomes 20% concentrate?
items.why: The concentrate is 25% of 12 = 3 liters and does not change. For it to be 20% of the total, the total must be 3 ÷ 0.20 = 15 liters, so add 15 − 12 = 3 liters of water. 15 liters is the new total volume, not the water to add.

items.q: A store mixes 10 kg of rice costing ₱50 per kg with 15 kg of rice costing ₱40 per kg. What is the cost per kilogram of the mixture?
items.why: Total cost: 10 × ₱50 + 15 × ₱40 = ₱500 + ₱600 = ₱1,100 for 25 kg, so ₱1,100 ÷ 25 = ₱44 per kg. Taking the simple average of ₱50 and ₱40 (₱45) ignores that there is more of the cheaper rice.

items.q: Joy's scores in four quizzes are 85, 90, 78 and 92. What score must she get on the fifth quiz to have an average of 88 for all five?
items.why: An average of 88 over five quizzes needs a total of 5 × 88 = 440. Her four scores add up to 85 + 90 + 78 + 92 = 345, so she needs 440 − 345 = 95. Answering 88 assumes the fifth score only has to equal the target average.

items.q: A municipality has a ₱12,000,000 development fund. It gives 40% to infrastructure and 25% to health, and splits the rest equally between education and agriculture. How much goes to education?
items.why: Infrastructure and health take 40% + 25% = 65%, leaving 35%. Education gets half of that, 17.5%: ₱12,000,000 × 0.175 = ₱2,100,000. ₱4,200,000 is the whole remainder before splitting it, and ₱3,000,000 is the health share.

items.q: A barangay divides ₱450,000 among three puroks in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How much does the purok with the largest share receive?
items.why: There are 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts, so one part is ₱450,000 ÷ 9 = ₱50,000. The largest share is 4 × ₱50,000 = ₱200,000. ₱150,000 is an equal three-way split (and also the middle share), and ₱100,000 is the smallest share.

items.q: A provincial office has 240 employees, and 45% of them are women. How many of the employees are men?
items.why: Men make up 100% − 45% = 55% of the staff: 240 × 0.55 = 132. 108 is the number of women (45% of 240), which answers the wrong question.

items.q: A sari-sari store sells a can of sardines for ₱39, which is the cost plus a 30% markup on cost. What is the cost of one can?
items.why: Selling price = cost × 1.30, so cost = ₱39 ÷ 1.3 = ₱30 (check: ₱30 + 30% of ₱30 = ₱39). Taking 30% off the selling price (₱39 × 0.70 = ₱27.30) is the trap, because the markup is based on cost, not on the selling price.

items.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to the word in capital letters: The barangay captain gave a TERSE reply to the reporter's question.
items.why: Terse means using very few words, often in a curt way. 'Angry and loud' is tempting because a terse reply can sound unfriendly, but the word describes length and bluntness, not volume or anger.

items.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to the word in capital letters: The new procedure will EXPEDITE the release of business permits.
items.why: To expedite is to make a process happen faster. 'Delay' is the opposite, and 'examine closely' describes a review, not a change in speed.

items.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to the word in capital letters: Her account of the flood was so METICULOUS that the engineers used it in their technical report.
choices: careful and exact in every detail
items.why: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail. The context supports this: engineers would use an account because it is precise. 'Emotional and moving' fits a dramatic story, but that would not make it useful for a technical report.

items.q: Which word is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'frugal'?
items.why: Frugal means sparing with money or resources, so its opposite is wasteful. 'Thrifty' is a synonym, which is the usual trap when a question asks for the opposite.

items.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to the word in capital letters: The treasurer's long explanation only served to OBFUSCATE the issue.
items.why: To obfuscate is to make something confusing or hard to understand. 'Simplify' is the exact opposite, and the phrase 'only served to' signals that the explanation made things worse, not better.

items.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to the word in capital letters: Despite repeated warnings, the vendor remained RECALCITRANT about moving his stall off the sidewalk.
items.why: Recalcitrant describes someone who stubbornly refuses to obey or cooperate. 'Unaware of the rule' does not fit because the vendor had received repeated warnings, so he knew the rule and still resisted.

items.q: Ano ang kahulugan ng salitang nasa malalaking titik? MASIGASIG si Aling Rosa sa pag-aalaga ng kaniyang halamanan kahit tag-init.
items.why: Masigasig means diligent and persistent, working hard at something. 'Tamad at mabagal' (lazy and slow) is its opposite, and the clue 'kahit tag-init' (even in the hot season) shows she keeps working despite difficulty.

items.q: Ano ang kahulugan ng salitang nasa malalaking titik? Hindi MAIKAKAILA ng kalihim na nahuli siya sa pagsusumite ng ulat.
items.why: Maikakaila comes from 'kaila' (to deny or hide), so 'hindi maikakaila' means 'cannot deny'. 'Maipapaliwanag' (can be explained) is tempting because the secretary might explain the delay, but the sentence is about being unable to deny it.

items.q: Alin ang KASALUNGAT ng salitang 'marangya' sa pangungusap: Marangya ang handaan sa kaarawan ng anak ng negosyante.
items.why: Marangya means lavish or luxurious, so its opposite is payak (simple, plain). 'Magarbo' and 'maluho' are synonyms of marangya, the usual trap in an opposite-meaning item.

items.q: Ano ang kahulugan ng salitang nasa malalaking titik? NAGPUPUYOS ang kaniyang damdamin nang malaman niyang ninakaw ang kaniyang bisikleta.
items.why: Nagpupuyos describes a feeling that burns or rages, usually anger. 'Nalulungkot nang tahimik' (quietly sad) is a possible reaction to theft, but puyos suggests intense, burning emotion, not quiet sadness.

items.q: The municipal office will remain closed on Monday ______ the typhoon signal is lifted before noon.
items.why: 'Unless' introduces the one condition under which the office would open: the closure stands except if the signal is lifted. 'Because' would make the lifting of the signal the reason for closing, which is illogical.

items.q: Neither the clerk nor the supervisors ______ aware of the new memo.
items.why: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Supervisors' is plural, so the plural past form 'were' is correct. 'Was' would agree with 'clerk', which is the farther subject.

items.q: By the time the rescue team arrived, the floodwater ______ to waist level.
items.why: 'By the time' plus a past event (arrived) calls for the past perfect, which shows an action completed before another past action. 'Has risen' is present perfect and does not fit a sequence set entirely in the past.

items.q: Ms. Galang has been working at the municipal hall ______ seven years.
items.why: Use 'for' with a length of time (seven years) and 'since' with a starting point (since 2019). 'Since' is the common trap because it also goes with the present perfect, but it cannot take a duration.

items.q: The mayor's speech was so ______ that even residents who had opposed the project began to nod in agreement.
items.why: Opponents starting to agree shows the speech convinced them, so 'persuasive' fits. 'Ambiguous' might explain mixed reactions, but an unclear speech would not win over people who had opposed the project.

items.q: Because the evidence against the accused was only ______, the judge said it could not by itself support a conviction.
items.why: Circumstantial evidence suggests a fact indirectly, so it may be too weak alone to convict. 'Only' and 'could not by itself' point to weak evidence; 'conclusive', 'irrefutable' and 'overwhelming' all describe strong evidence and contradict the sentence.

items.q: ______ malakas ang ulan, itinuloy pa rin ng mga mag-aaral ang paglilinis ng plaza.
items.why: 'Bagaman' (although) shows contrast: the students continued despite the heavy rain, which matches 'pa rin' (still). 'Dahil' (because) would make the rain the reason for continuing, which is illogical.

items.q: ______ ng pandesal si Mang Ernesto tuwing umaga mula pa noong isang taon.
items.why: 'Tuwing umaga' (every morning) and 'mula pa noong isang taon' (since last year) describe a habit that is still going on, so the imperfective aspect 'bumibili' is needed. 'Bumili' is completed aspect and cannot express a continuing habit.

items.q: Ipinagpaliban ang pulong ng sangguniang barangay ______ hindi dumating ang karamihan sa mga kagawad.
items.why: 'Sapagkat' (because) gives the reason for the postponement: most councilors did not come. 'Ngunit' (but) signals contrast, yet there is nothing contrasting between a postponement and the absence of members.

items.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? '(A) Each of the volunteers were (B) given a raincoat (C) and a flashlight (D) before the evacuation drill.'
items.why: The subject is 'each', which is singular, so the verb should be 'was'. The plural 'volunteers' sits next to the verb and makes 'were' sound right, which is the trap.

items.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? '(A) Mr. Dizon asked (B) my brother and I (C) to help him carry (D) the sacks of rice.'
items.why: 'My brother and I' is the object of 'asked', so the object pronoun 'me' is required: 'asked my brother and me'. A quick test: drop 'my brother and' and you would say 'asked me', not 'asked I'.

items.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? '(A) Last Saturday, the residents (B) of Purok 3 (C) clean the drainage canal (D) along Mabini Street.'
items.why: 'Last Saturday' places the action in the past, so the verb must be 'cleaned'. The other parts are correct; the time marker in part A is what makes the present-tense verb wrong.

items.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? '(A) Of the two proposals, (B) the one submitted by (C) Engineer Salonga is (D) the most practical.'
items.why: When only two things are compared, use the comparative form: 'the more practical'. The superlative 'most' is for three or more, and part A ('Of the two proposals') is the clue.

items.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? '(A) After the long night shift, (B) the nurse went home (C) and laid down (D) for an hour.'
items.why: The nurse is resting, not placing an object, so the verb is 'lie', whose past tense is 'lay': 'and lay down'. 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (to put something down) and needs an object, as in 'laid the bag down'.

items.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? '(A) The supervisor insisted for (B) the immediate submission (C) of all time records (D) by the end of the month.'
choices: (D) by the end of the month
items.why: The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on': 'insisted on the immediate submission'. 'Insisted for' is a common local error, perhaps influenced by 'asked for'.

items.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? '(A) Neither of the two applicants (B) have completed (C) the required training (D) for the position.'
items.why: 'Neither' used as a pronoun is singular, so the verb should be 'has completed'. The plural noun 'applicants' inside the 'of' phrase is not the subject.

items.q: Aling bahagi ng pangungusap ang may mali? '(A) Upang marinig ng lahat, (B) lumapit sa mikropono (C) ang kapitan at (D) nagsalita ng malakas.'
items.why: 'Nang' is used to show how an action is done (manner), so it should be 'nagsalita nang malakas'. 'Ng' in part A is correct because it marks the doer of 'marinig' ('ng lahat').

items.q: Aling bahagi ng pangungusap ang may mali? '(A) Dumalo sa pulong (B) ang kalihim ng barangay, (C) at dumalo din (D) ang ingat-yaman.'
items.why: In standard Filipino, 'rin' follows a word ending in a vowel (or w/y) and 'din' follows a consonant. 'Dumalo' ends in the vowel o, so it should be 'dumalo rin'.

items.q: Which sentence is correctly constructed?
choices: Walking along Rizal Avenue, the new mall caught my attention.
Walking along Rizal Avenue, the new mall was noticed by me.
The new mall caught my attention, walking along Rizal Avenue.
While walking along Rizal Avenue, I noticed the new mall.
items.why: The modifier 'walking along Rizal Avenue' must attach to the person who walked. Only the last sentence makes 'I' the subject. The other three make it sound as if the mall was walking (a dangling modifier).

items.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
choices: The power went out at noon; the generator started a few seconds later.
The power went out at noon, the generator started a few seconds later.
The power went out at noon the generator started a few seconds later.
The power went out at noon, then the generator started a few seconds later.
items.why: Two independent clauses can be joined by a semicolon. A comma alone creates a comma splice, no punctuation creates a run-on, and 'then' is an adverb, not a conjunction, so ', then' is still a comma splice.

items.q: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly?
choices: The training covers first aid, how to evacuate, and to communicate during emergencies.
The training covers giving first aid, evacuation, and to communicate during emergencies.
The training covers first aid, evacuation, and emergency communication.
The training covers first aid, evacuating, and how communication works in emergencies.
items.why: Items in a series should share the same grammatical form. The correct sentence lists three nouns (first aid, evacuation, communication). The others mix nouns, gerunds, infinitives and clauses.

items.q: Which sentence places its modifier correctly so that the meaning is clear?
choices: The clerk returned the form to the applicant with a missing signature.
The clerk returned to the applicant the form that had a missing signature.
With a missing signature, the clerk returned the form to the applicant.
The clerk with a missing signature returned the form to the applicant.
items.why: The missing signature belongs to the form, and only the second sentence puts the modifier right next to 'the form'. The first sentence suggests the applicant is missing a signature, and the last two attach it to the clerk.

items.q: Which of the following is a complete sentence?
choices: Because the bridge was closed for repairs.
The bridge, which was closed for repairs after the earthquake.
Closed for repairs after the earthquake last July.
The bridge was closed for repairs after the earthquake.
items.why: A complete sentence needs a subject and a main verb and must express a complete thought. The first is a dependent clause, the second has a subject but no main verb, and the third has no subject.

items.q: Which sentence states the idea most clearly, with no ambiguous pronoun?
choices: Mrs. Reyes told Ms. Tan, "Your application has been approved."
When Mrs. Reyes met Ms. Tan, she told her that her application was approved.
Mrs. Reyes told Ms. Tan that her application had been approved by her.
She told Ms. Tan, Mrs. Reyes, that her application had been approved.
items.why: The direct quotation makes it plain whose application was approved: Ms. Tan's. In the other sentences, 'she' and 'her' could refer to either woman.

items.q: Which sentence follows the standard order of adjectives in English?
choices: She bought a red small plastic basin.
She bought a plastic small red basin.
She bought a small red plastic basin.
She bought a small plastic red basin.
items.why: English adjectives usually follow the order size, then color, then material: small, red, plastic. The last choice gets size first but puts material before color.

items.q: What is the most logical order of the sentences?
items.why: Sentence 3 introduces the topic, then the signal words give the sequence: 'First' (2), 'Next' (4), and 'After paying' (1), which must follow the payment in 4.

items.q: What is the most logical order of the sentences?
items.why: Sentence 2 states the problem and 4 explains it ('them' refers to the families). 'Because of this' (1) introduces the response, and 'These early alerts' (3) must come after the alerts are mentioned in 1.

items.q: What is the most logical order of the sentences?
items.why: The paragraph moves from problem (2) to solution (4, 'To solve the problem'), to the immediate effect (3, enough change on hand), to the final result (1, sales doubled). Putting 1 before 3 reports the outcome before the change that caused it.

items.q: What is the most logical order of the sentences?
items.why: Sentence 3 is the topic sentence. 'First' (1) gives the first benefit and 'also' (4) adds another, and 'For these reasons' (2) concludes after all the reasons are given.

items.q: What is the most logical order of the sentences?
items.why: The announcement (4) comes first, then the officials' reason for it (1). 'However' (3) introduces the drivers' objection to that reason, and the agreement (2) resolves the dispute at the end.

items.q: What is the most logical order of the sentences?
items.why: In sentence 2, 'Instead' and 'they' refer back to the used sheets in sentence 4, so 4 must come right before 2. The paragraph opens with the program (1) and ends with the fix and its result (3).

items.q: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
choices: A barangay's rainwater program overcame early doubts and grew once residents saw its benefits.
Dengue mosquitoes are the main danger of storing water at home.
The town water district failed to supply Barangay Talisay during the summer.
Councilor Bautista deserves an award for her proposal.
items.why: The passage follows the program from its proposal, through early doubts, to its growth after the first season. The water district and the dengue worry are details, and the passage never says the councilor deserves an award.

items.q: According to the passage, what did a household have to do to receive a drum?
choices: Pay a small fee to the council
items.why: The passage states that each household that attended a two-hour seminar would receive a drum. The drum already came with a mesh filter, and gutter cleaning was something taught in the seminar, not a requirement.

items.q: Which of the following can best be inferred about why more families joined the second round of seminars?
choices: The council made the seminar shorter.
The barangay required every household to join.
Reports from the first participants about buying less water persuaded others.
Dengue cases in the barangay dropped sharply.
items.why: Right after describing the savings, the passage says 'Their stories spread quickly' and that more families joined. Nothing is said about a shorter seminar, a requirement, or dengue figures.

items.q: What problem were the two walk-in windows meant to address?
choices: The website stopped working during busy hours.
Text messages were not reaching applicants.
Relatives were charging high fees to book slots.
Applicants who could not easily book online were being sent home.
items.why: The passage says some applicants arrived without an appointment and were asked to come back another day, and the walk-in windows followed the complaints. The passage mentions relatives booking slots for pay, but not that the fees were high or that this was the problem being fixed.

items.q: Which best describes the attitude of the head of the office toward the new system?
choices: Realistic about its flaws but convinced it is an improvement
Regretful about replacing the old line
Indifferent to the needs of elderly applicants
items.why: She 'admits the system is still imperfect' yet argues the old line was harder on the elderly. Admitting flaws rules out 'dismissive', and her concern for elderly applicants rules out 'indifferent'.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as part of the online appointment system?
choices: Receiving a text message confirming the time
items.why: The passage describes choosing a slot on the municipal website and getting a text confirmation, but it never mentions paying fees online. Readers may assume online payment because many systems include it.

items.q: According to the passage, why do families who earn a daily wage often prefer sachets?
choices: Sachets cost less per gram than large bottles.
Sachets let them buy only what they can afford that day.
Sachets are easier to recycle than bottles.
Large bottles are not sold in sari-sari stores.
items.why: The passage says the sachet 'lets them buy only what they can afford that day'. The first choice is the trap: the passage says the price per gram is actually higher than that of a large bottle.

items.q: The author mentions the store owners' complaint mainly to show that
choices: banning sachets in one town may only shift the buying to another town
store owners earn more from sachets than from bottles
customers prefer large bottles to sachets
items.why: The complaint is that customers 'simply buy the same products in the next town', which shows a local ban does not reduce sachet use. Nothing in the passage compares store owners' earnings or reports manufacturers' views on refill stations.

items.q: With which statement would the author most likely agree?
choices: Refill stations will surely replace sachets within a few years.
Sachets should be banned nationwide at once.
Families should stop buying products in small amounts.
Refill stations can spread only if they stay as convenient and cheap as sachets.
items.why: The last sentence says the spread of refill stations depends on whether they remain as convenient and cheap as sachets. The author calls them 'more promising', not certain, and describes buying small amounts as sensible for daily-wage families.

items.q: What is the main point of the passage?
choices: Stores in the town never keep enough candles.
Grandchildren should always obey their grandparents.
Lola Pacing's careful preparation, once teased, proved its worth and was taken up by her family.
Typhoons in the town usually cause blackouts that last nine days.
items.why: The passage moves from the grandchildren teasing her, to the typhoon that proved her right, to the grandson continuing the habit. The moral about obeying grandparents is never stated, and the nine-day blackout happened once, not usually.

items.q: The sentence 'They stopped laughing the year a strong typhoon cut the power' suggests that the grandchildren
choices: came to see the value of her preparations
were too frightened by the storm to speak
lost interest in the biscuit tin
items.why: During the blackout, Lola Pacing had light and dry documents while neighbors had none, and later her grandson took over the yearly check. This shows a change of mind, not fear or loss of interest.

items.q: Ayon sa teksto, ano ang dahilan kung bakit sinimulan ang gulayan sa barangay?
choices: Upang magkaroon ng kita ang sangguniang barangay
Upang magamit ang compost mula sa tirang pagkain
Dahil maraming pamilya ang hindi makabili ng sapat na gulay
items.why: The first paragraph says the captain noticed many families could no longer buy enough vegetables, so the council turned the vacant lot into a garden. Selling surplus and making compost came later and were not the reason the project started.

items.q: Ano ang naging tulong ng agriculturist mula sa munisipyo?
choices: Tinuruan niya ang mga residente na gumawa ng compost.
Itinaboy niya ang mga ligaw na manok.
Nagbigay siya ng binhi ng pechay, talong, at sitaw.
Siya ang nagdilig ng mga halaman tuwing umaga.
items.why: The passage says that with the agriculturist's help, residents learned to make compost from food scraps and dry leaves. Seeds are bought with the garden's income, and the residents themselves took turns watering.

items.q: Para kay Kapitana Lorna, ano ang pinakamahalagang naibigay ng proyekto bukod sa pagkain?
choices: Ang malaking kita mula sa pagbebenta ng gulay
Ang pagkatuto ng mga residente sa pagtatanim
Ang paggamit ng bakanteng lote sa likod ng covered court
items.why: The last sentence says the project gave more than food: neighbors learned to help one another again. Learning to farm is true but is not what she names, and the passage says the produce sells at a low price, not for big profit.
